features.feature_value: Removes posts when language becomes name-calling/insulting individuals or groups; pair treated as removable together.
features.evidence_span: "name-calling or insulting individuals or a whole group, I removed them"
features.rationale: The participant explicitly links insulting/name-calling to their removal decision, including handling mismatched mirroring.

features.feature_value: Gets rid of posts with cuss words and those targeting individuals in ways that could lead to harm.
features.evidence_span: "calling the other side cuss words" / "targeted individual people... could lead to harm"
features.rationale: They state specific language types (swearing) and personal targeting/harm as criteria for removal.

features.feature_value: Assesses intensity of wording, its effect on others, and whether it adds to a meaningful debate.
features.evidence_span: "intensity of the words used" / "add anything to a meaningful debate"
features.rationale: They describe a deliberative evaluation framework tied to intensity, impact, and debate contribution.

features.feature_value: Decides based on whether one post is more extreme than the other.
features.evidence_span: "seeing if one was more extreme than the other"
features.rationale: Their criterion is directly comparative across the pair (extremity differential).

features.feature_value: Keeps posts that stay cordial; removes when there is swearing or too much attacking of the other side.
features.evidence_span: "keep things pretty cordial. not swearing and not attacking"
features.rationale: They use a social-norm threshold (cordial/no swearing/no heavy attacks) to guide keep decisions.

features.feature_value: Reflection reduces decision impact to foul language.
features.rationale: Although brief, it clearly identifies foul language as the salient influence.

features.feature_value: Evaluates whether posts cover the same topic while taking opposing views.
features.evidence_span: "Were the posts about the same topic" / "taking opposing views"
features.rationale: They describe the key pair-level comparison they used (topic match + opposition).

features.feature_value: Notes that some pairs appear reinstated together (treated as a unit across versions).
features.evidence_span: "Some pairs are obviously reinstated the other statement."
features.rationale: They refer to how mirror statements behave in the pair and how that affects inclusion beyond content-only criteria.
